title: Obliviousness of the candidate
statement: Let $W$ and $M$ be finite machines over the binary alphabet, and let $a\in\mathbb{N}$. For any two binary inputs of equal length and every time $t\in\mathbb{N}$, the candidate built from $W$, $M$, and $a$ has the same input-head position and the same work-tape head positions on both inputs.
hypotheses_covered: Two binary inputs of equal length
replaced:
For all binary machines $W$ and $M$ and every padding constant $a$, the candidate
simulator built from $W$, $M$, and $a$ is oblivious: its head positions at every time
step depend only on the length of the input.  This holds on all binary inputs of every
length, including the empty input, and uses no assumption about the computations of
$W$ or $M$.
